title: Thai Eggplant Stir-Fry
subtitle: with Vermicelli Noodles
description: Make winter brighter with this nourishing bowl of veggies, peanuts and vermicelli noodles. The old saying that 'we eat with our eyes first' certainly rings true here.

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Bring a small saucepan of water to the boil for the eggs. Cut the eggplant into 2cm chunks (see Kitchen notes). Finely chop the capsicum, discarding the seeds. Trim the beans and cut into 2cm lengths. Coarsely chop the peanuts. Pick the mint leaves, discarding the stems (see Kitchen notes).

Boil eggs: Cook 2 eggs in the pan of boiling water for 7 mins for soft-boiled, or 8 mins for hard-boiled. Drain, then cool in cold water. Peel and halve the eggs. Meanwhile, put the noodles in a large heatproof bowl, cover with boiling water and soak for 5 mins or until tender. Drain, then season with salt.

Stir-fry eggplant: Heat 1½ tbs vegetable oil in a large frypan over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the eggplant and ¼ tsp chilli flakes, if using, for 6-8 mins until soft. Meanwhile, put 1½ tsp cornflour, 2 tbs water, 1½ tbs soy sauce, 3 tsp tomato sauce, 1 tsp white vinegar and 1½ tsp honey in a small bowl and stir well to combine.

Add veggies and sauce: Add the capsicum and beans to the eggplant and stir-fry for 2 mins. Add the soy sauce mixture and stir-fry for a further 1 min or until the veggies are tender and the sauce is thickened. Remove the pan from the heat and stir in half the mint.
Serve up: Divide the noodles, stir-fried veggies and eggs among bowls. Scatter over the peanuts and remaining mint and enjoy.

Kitchen notes: Only 300g (3½ cups) eggplant is needed for this recipe, so if your eggplant looks very large, you may want to check this. Either weigh it or fill a measuring jug with the chopped eggplant for a quick way to measure. ~ We've substituted mint for the Thai basil pictured due to availability. Don't worry, the dish will be just as delicious!
